beats.narration: Module four. Your agents work — you built them over the last two modules. This module is about proving they keep working under production traffic. Because development hides the failures that production reveals: the input shape nobody tested, the rate limit at peak, the fetched page carrying a hidden instruction.

items.text: the fetched page with a hidden instruction

beats.narration: By the end, five things. You'll write an eval suite that defines done before you ship, scored by a judge you calibrated. You'll build tests and traces that catch a regression and point at the exact step that broke. You'll separate retriable failures from terminal ones, so the system degrades instead of crashing. You'll keep everything inside a cost and latency budget, even with several agents coordinating. And you'll defend it all against prompt injection and untrusted input, well enough to survive a security review.

items.text: 2. tests + traces → the exact step that broke

beats.narration: One idea runs through everything here. When production fails, it's almost never a bug in the code that ran. It's a decision that was never made. Success was never written down as a graded set. The retriable case was never given a path. The budget was never instrumented. The boundary was never enforced. So this module makes each decision on paper, before the failure shows up live.
